children.name: in 1924, following San Diego's 1915 Panama-California Exposition, George Marston commissioned architects Lincoln Rogers and Frank Stevenson to design a building that would become a turning point in city architectural history.
children.characters: in 1924, following San Diego's 1915 Panama-California Exposition, George Marston commissioned architects Lincoln Rogers and Frank Stevenson to design a building that would become a turning point in city architectural history.

children.name: The Italian Renaissance Revival style structure they created had a  symmetrical composition, richly articulated masonry, arched openings, and generously proportioned public rooms that expressed permanence, dignity, and civic generosity. Some things never change.

children.name: After the YMCA closed its doors, the downtown landmark slumbered until it was reimagined as The Guild, part of the Marriott’s Tribute Portfolio. The luxury hotel served as a central oasis for the ever-growing numbers of visitors to “America’s Finest City”.

children.name: Ownership rejuvenates The Guild with a refreshed interior design, sparkling new pool, private art collection, and exciting food and beverage offerings including Zuma that draw locals and international visitors alike. Spa and wellness menus and facilities make the hotel a true urban resort and destination.

children.name: 500 W. Broadway, built when San Diego’s identity was tightly tied to its waterfront and naval presence, was an Italian Renaissance masterwork that became a place of welcome and belonging for a growing military community. As a YMCA, it was a civic institution that offered lodging, recreation, education and fellowship. Today, we’re proud stewards of that spirit of service, camaraderie and hospitality.

children.name: In 1924, George Marsden saw more than a building. He imagined a grand center of city life, a gathering place to elevate hospitality and raise a downtown. The Italian Renaissance icon he built welcomed and entertained some eight million servicemen and women. The Guild preserves the existing structure, retains defining architectural elements, and incorporates materials that will age gracefully,  extending the life of this important civic landmark.
